exposure: Vitamin D supplement use during pregnancy
number of daytime hours spent outdoors
outcome: prevalence of Vitamin D deficiency (<20 ng/mL)
prevalence of Vitamin D insufficiency (21-29 ng/mL)
cohort: The study included 166 pregnant women and their newborns in Lagos, Nigeria.
finding: The study found that despite a low prevalence of Vitamin D deficiency in mothers (4.8%), their neonates had a significantly higher deficiency rate (29.5%), and maternal Vitamin D status was associated with supplement use, outdoor exposure, and dressing style.
cross-section timing: during pregnancy and at birth (cord blood)
